1	# Releasing Brain
2	
3	Brain releases the same way Graph does: a tag triggers a build of every target,
4	the binaries and their checksums are attached to a GitHub release, and a nightly
5	prerelease is cut from `main` each morning.
6	
7	## Cutting a release
8	
9	1. Move the work into a `## [X.Y.Z]` section in `CHANGELOG.md`, dated.
10	2. Tag and push:
11	
12	   ```sh
13	   git tag vX.Y.Z
14	   git push origin vX.Y.Z
15	   ```
16	
17	`.github/workflows/release.yml` does the rest: it builds `linux`, `darwin`, and
18	`windows` for both `amd64` and `arm64`, packages each as a `.tar.gz` (`.zip` on
19	Windows), writes `checksums.txt`, and creates the release with generated notes.
20	Re-running it against an existing tag updates that release rather than failing.
21	
22	You can also run it from the Actions tab with a version, which is the way to
23	re-cut a release whose upload failed.
24	
25	### Why one runner builds everything
26	
27	Brain's default build is pure Go — both the SQLite driver and the vector path
28	have cgo-free implementations (`internal/cli/sqlite_driver_purego.go`,
29	`internal/cli/embed_vec_purego.go`), and SQLite itself comes from
30	`modernc.org/sqlite` rather than a C binding — so `CGO_ENABLED=0`
31	cross-compiles every target from one Linux runner.
32	Graph needs a runner per OS because its tree-sitter bindings need cgo. The
33	release workflow asserts this rather than assuming it:
34	
35	```yaml
36	- name: Verify the default build needs no cgo
37	  run: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/entire-brain
38	```
39	
40	If someone adds a cgo dependency to the default build, that step fails and the
41	release stops, instead of silently producing binaries that only run on the
42	build host.
43	
44	The `brain_cgo` build tag still exists for the native embedder. It is not part
45	of a release build.
46	
47	### Windows verification
48	
49	Cross-compiling from one runner means the release path never executes a
50	Windows binary, and `test.yml`'s Windows suite runs with `CGO_ENABLED=1`
51	because the race detector needs cgo — not the pure-Go configuration that
52	ships. Both `release.yml` and `nightly.yml` therefore gate publishing on a
53	`verify windows` job on a Depot Windows runner (hosted `windows-latest` is
54	2-core on private repos and cannot finish `internal/cli` in one binary within
55	a reasonable budget — note this puts a Depot dependency on the publish path):
56	it runs `go test ./...` with
57	`CGO_ENABLED=0` and smoke-runs the CLI (`version`, `capabilities --json`, a
58	`remember`/`recall` roundtrip in a scratch repo) via `tools/windows-sanity.ps1`.
59	The release job runs the script against the actual `windows/amd64` artifact it
60	is about to publish; the nightly verifies its own equivalent build, because the
61	nightly builds and publishes in a single job. `windows/arm64` is still only
62	cross-compiled — no amd64 runner can execute it.
63	
64	## Nightlies
65	
66	`.github/workflows/nightly.yml` runs at 06:00 UTC, matching Graph, and tags
67	`vX.Y.Z-nightly.<timestamp>.<sha>` where `X.Y.Z` is the newest version in the
68	changelog.
69	
70	It skips days `main` has not moved. A dated prerelease that is byte-identical to
71	yesterday's makes "which nightly has the fix" harder to answer, not easier, so
72	the run checks whether the newest prerelease already points at `HEAD` and exits
73	if it does.
74	
75	## Pull requests build the release path
76	
77	`release.yml` also runs on pull requests that change it. That run builds every
78	target and skips the publish job, so a change to the release process is proven
79	on the PR rather than on the tag that depends on it.
80	
81	## What may be claimed in release material
82	
83	`mise run release:readiness` reports which claims the retained evidence
84	supports. It classifies every track as one of `proven`, `local-gated`,
85	`pending-retained-proof`, `pending-target-evidence`, or `no-claim`, and the gate
86	fails when release material asserts something the evidence does not carry.
87	
88	Run it before writing an announcement, and treat anything short of `proven` as
89	not sayable.
90	
91	## Install channels
92	
93	Releases reach users three ways:
94	
95	| channel | resolves through |
96	|---|---|
97	| `entire plugin install brain` | the [plugin index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index) |
98	| `scripts/get-brain.sh` | the GitHub releases API, verifying `checksums.txt` |
99	| a downloaded archive | the release page |
100	
101	The installer verifies the downloaded archive against `checksums.txt` and exits
102	non-zero on a mismatch. A missing checksum file is a warning; a wrong checksum
103	is fatal.

# Changelog

All notable changes to `entire-brain` are recorded here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.3.0] - 2026-10-26

### Removed

- The one-time migrations for Brain's old code stores. Refresh, code inspection,
  and bundle operations now refuse old layouts with recovery instructions;
  status and doctor report the same problem. Run `entire brain refresh index`
  with entire-brain 0.2.0 once before upgrading to preserve runtime traces, or
  back up and remove the brain directory and refresh to rebuild. Legacy vector
  detection remains in place for health and privacy checks.

### Changed

- Releases no longer re-prove retained performance evidence at tag time. The
  `release-evidence` job moved from the `test` workflow (where it ran on `v*`
  tags and blocked publishing) to a dispatch-only `evidence` workflow. Evidence
  is a point-in-time record: each manifest names the `source_head` it measured,
  every `mise run <lane>:evidence:update` audits with `--fail-on-flags` before
  writing reports, and the timed distill lanes' corpora are machine-bound, so
  re-measuring at every tag made releases wait on measurements the release did
  not change. Tagging now only builds, verifies, and publishes binaries.

- Re-recorded the Radar tool-contract evidence and the current-repo distill
  scheduler evidence against current main (median 1.89x of five pairs vs the
  1.25x floor, measured on a fresh zero-fact store so reconcile stays quiet).
  The large-repo distill lane still carries its September record; its corpus
  (a 2,375-session local brain store) exists only on the original recorder's
  machine.

### Fixed

- The sessions export no longer stalls for hours on a host CLI whose remote
  metadata fetch times out per checkpoint (entireio/cli#2902: 319 routed
  checkpoints × a 120s fetch deadline read as a `setup` hang). After three
  consecutive `checkpoint explain` reads each over 60 seconds, a circuit
  breaker stops asking, folds every skipped checkpoint into one counted
  warning naming the cause and the remedy, and the export finishes degraded
  in minutes. Validation tracked in COR-2277.

- A first `setup` no longer ends on `freshness: degraded`. The agent wiring
  files setup itself writes — `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the PreToolUse
  entry in `.claude/settings.json` — no longer count as a dirty worktree in the
  live state report, the same exemption the dirty-worktree gate already
  applied. The files stay in the indexed corpus.

- `status --fail-on degraded` and `--fail-on unsafe` no longer pass without
  looking when the brain has no semantic assessment: a degraded or unsafe
  retrieval freshness now trips the gate even when no graph provider is
  installed. A healthy retrieval report still does not substitute for the
  missing assessment, so `--fail-on release` keeps failing on unindexed brains.

- `mise run release:smoke` leg 1 gates on `--fail-on release` instead of
  `--fail-on degraded`, so a runner without the entire-graph provider fails

#!/bin/bash
#MISE description="Release smoke: full user journey on scratch repos (enable, capture, distill, recall, graph, hosted sync up/down)"
#
# A tripwire, not a test suite: one assert per leg, each fails loudly.
# Legs: 1 setup, 2 checkpoint capture, 3 distill, 4 recall, 5 graph query,
#        6 hosted upload (staging), 7 pull+merge on a second clone.
#
# The entire-brain binary under test is built from this checkout (the RC SHA);
# the host `entire` CLI and the entire-graph provider are the installed ones.
# Brain state is isolated per "machine" via ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR, like
# scripts/hosted-sync-smoke.sh; HOME and the host CLI's login stay real because
# legs 3 and 6 need the real coding agent and the real staging auth.
#
# Environment the runner must export (legs 6-7; never hardcode secrets):
#   REPO_ID       region-local repo ULID of a STAGING brainstore repo
#   API_URL       that repo's home-cell base URL, e.g. https://<home-cell>.api.partial.to/api/v1
#   AUTH_CONTEXT  optional saved `entire auth` login to mint the token from
#                 (e.g. us.auth.partial.to); default: the active context
#   ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN  optional prebuilt entire-brain binary (skips go build)
#
# Evidence: a timestamped pass/fail summary (with brain/graph/host versions)

--- 84fd0b41 fix(cli): stop hosted facts sync retrying 403 forever on a stale repo binding
A binding written by 'entire brain connect' never refreshed, so once the
bound repo was deleted or the caller lost access, every trigger (session-end
hook, daemon tick, push hint) retried the same 403 indefinitely and tripped
brainstore's auth-failure monitor (COR-2279).

factsync now surfaces 403 as ErrNoAccess. On a pull denial the sync
re-resolves placement once: a different repo id in the same cell (deleted
and re-onboarded) rebinds and retries; otherwise the binding records a 24h
no-access pause that all background triggers skip, with one actionable line
naming connect. connect clears the pause by writing a fresh binding; status
reports it.

A push-only 403 keeps the pull-only degradation: a read-only grant
(push 403, pull 200) is a working state and must keep pulling. Rebind
requires the same cell URL so explicit staging/non-default bindings are
never retargeted. 401 keeps its current behavior so auth-plumbing breaks
still reach the monitor.

disconnect changed the binding) or failed. Now the paused line prints only
